clue.text: Degree - university exam success - worker’s topic in French literature?

blocks.note: Master of Arts, a university degree
standard abbreviation
to succeed in an exam is to get a pass
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A student's academic record, ending with the subject of a worker's French literature essay.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy de Maupassant was the nineteenth-century French short-story writer; the question mark admits that a writer is only a 'topic' for those studying him.
explanation.definitionFit: Students of French literature study Maupassant's short stories, so the author himself is a subject on the syllabus.

clue.text: I intended to skip Australia after embracing bloke dwelling within

indicators.note: to skip something is to leave it out, so the letter for Australia is dropped
an embrace wraps around, so the shortened word holds the bloke inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
what you intended is what you meant
A is the international vehicle code for Australia; removed
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they meant to bypass Australia, having first hugged a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The bloke goes in after the first letter of the shortened word, not at its edge. Australia's A comes from its international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanent is a philosophical and theological term for something inherent, existing or operating inside rather than beyond.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink? Wary about sin

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for wary surrounds the word for sin

blocks.note: shy as in cautious or wary
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A puritan, wary of sin, wonders whether something is an alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wary' here means timid or reluctant, a sense of shy that is easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Andalusia, so it is one kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Modest prize money denied entrant in fourth place

indicators.note: to be denied something is to go without it, so one letter is refused and removed

blocks.note: a purse is the money put up as a prize, as in boxing
the letter standing fourth in the prize-money word, removed

explanation.surface: A contestant who finished fourth misses out on the modest prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: PURSE without its fourth letter S leaves PURE. 'Entrant in fourth place' sounds like a competitor but means the letter in that slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest in the sense of chaste or virtuous, which is one sense of pure.

clue.text: Unusual orange lily around the country

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare orange lily is found growing across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening regionally takes place in various parts or regions of a country rather than nationally.

clue.text: A flier manoeuvring round ring twice showing source of lift?

an aircraft manoeuvring changes its position, so these letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written
a ring is shaped like the letter O; twice gives two of them

explanation.surface: A pilot loops a ring twice, demonstrating where lift comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerofoil is the shaped wing section whose curved profile generates lift as air flows over it.

clue.text: Writer’s taken up line penned by outstanding mountain dweller

explanation.walkthrough: NEP then A(L)I. Writing A1 as AI is a common crossword licence for 'outstanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali comes from Nepal, the Himalayan country containing Everest, so is fairly called a mountain dweller.

clue.text: Kind charity people will show it

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.walkthrough: chari(TY PE)ople. 'Kind' reads as an adjective about the charity people but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind is a sort or category, the same as a type.

clue.text: A scoundrel keeping maiden quiet in charity home

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the scoundrel holds the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a louse is a contemptible person
M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over
the hushing exclamation

explanation.surface: A villain keeps a young woman quiet in a charitable institution, like a gothic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A + L(M SH)OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse was a house built by a charity to lodge poor or elderly people, so a charity home.

clue.text: Funereal music, say, in cathedral

Ely is the crossword's favourite cathedral city, in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Mournful music being played, for instance, inside a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: EL(EG)Y. Ely is a small English cathedral city, much used for its handy letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or musical piece, typically a lament for the dead, hence funereal.

clue.text: Prince affected manner that is plain

blocks.note: PR is a recognised abbreviation for prince
to put on airs is to adopt an affected manner
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A prince puts on airs, which is obvious to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' does double duty in the surface but here gives IE; 'plain' looks like an adjective (obvious) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, flat grassland of North America, so a plain in the geographical sense.

clue.text: I am critical of limiting old quarantine

indicators.note: limiting something sets bounds around it, so the critical word goes round

blocks.note: taken as written
to slate is to criticise harshly
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone admits criticising strict limits on old-style quarantine rules.
explanation.walkthrough: I + S(O)LATE; 'I am critical of' splits so that I stands alone and 'am critical of' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others, which is to isolate them.

clue.text: Prosecute meat company finally regarding quantities of fat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A legal action against a meat firm over the fat content of its products.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is hard animal fat, so suety describes something full of or like such fat.

clue.text: Unit’s soldiers holding position - ammunition here?

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the soldiers enclose the position

blocks.note: a band is a group or unit; the 's means has
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the lie of something is its position, as of a golf ball

explanation.surface: A military unit's troops hold a position, and one asks where the ammunition is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: BAND + O(LIE)R. The question mark flags a definition by example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder belt with loops or pockets for carrying cartridges, so ammunition is stored there.

clue.text: It’s no freighter - but it has quantities of cotton, dry inside, with it

indicators.note: inside places the dry letters within the quantities of cotton

blocks.note: cotton is packed and shipped in bales
TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A ship that isn't a cargo vessel, yet carries bales of cotton kept dry in its hold.
explanation.walkthrough: BA(TT)LES + HIP. The surface looks like a cargo inventory, which is exactly what this vessel is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a heavily armed warship, built for fighting rather than carrying goods, so it is no freighter.

clue.text: Performer elicits art when playing

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist gives recitals, solo concerts of music or readings, so is a kind of performer.

clue.text: Pregnancy service, clean, intact, in Luxembourg area after moving

clue.text: Note: idiot seen around endless affray is unidentified

clue.text: Square support in golf: heading for nice, slightly-reduced score?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: nine is a square number, three times three
a golf tee is the peg supporting the ball
first letter

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so one fewer is a score slightly reduced; the question mark flags this playful definition. 'Nice' lowercase here is the adjective, though the French city lurks.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is called a score, so the number one below it is a score cut down a little.

clue.text: Millions in the demo displaying heat?

blocks.note: taken as written
a rally is a mass demonstration
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Millions turn out at a protest that is getting heated.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + R(M)ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermally means by way of heat, so in a manner that shows or involves heat; the fit is loose adverbially.

clue.text: Recording anger about money in big business

ire is anger

clue.text: Party raver’s target of the munchies?

clue.text: Hungarian-born conductor held in adoration

clue.text: Runs through periods without leadership involving China

clue.text: Putting second half first, issue newspaper article
